# SvelteForge

Production-ready foundations for normal SvelteKit projects. SvelteForge is a `sv` community addon, not a framework replacement and not a separate component runtime. Generated source belongs to the consumer project.

## Stack

- SvelteKit + Svelte 5
- Skeleton UI v5 + Skeleton Svelte
- Tailwind CSS v4
- Paraglide FR/EN
- Vitest
- Dashboard option: Better Auth + Drizzle + PostgreSQL

## Templates

### Base

A lightweight application foundation with:

- essential SvelteForge primitives/UI/layout components
- complete Skeleton v5 theme
- dark/light mode
- SEO + sitemap helpers
- Paraglide FR/EN
- Vitest baseline
- generated agent/project context

### Dashboard

Everything in Base plus Better Auth, Drizzle/PostgreSQL, authenticated layouts, admin dashboard, users CRUD, settings and Zod validation patterns.

## UI reuse order

1. Existing SvelteForge primitives
2. Existing SvelteForge UI components
3. Existing SvelteForge layouts
4. Official `@skeletonlabs/skeleton-svelte` components
5. Create a new component only when no existing option fits

Skeleton is the UI foundation. Do not install or invent a parallel UI kit.

## Skeleton v5

Use current Skeleton v5 classes/presets:

- `preset-filled-*`
- `preset-tonal-*`
- `preset-outlined-*`
- component classes such as `btn`, `input`, `select`, `textarea`, `checkbox`, `badge`, `card`, `table`

Do not use obsolete/fake classes such as `variant-*`, `preset-ghost`, or Bootstrap-style `alert alert-*`.

## CSS architecture

The scaffold deliberately has only two CSS responsibilities:

```text
src/routes/layout.css
└── single global CSS entrypoint
    ├── Tailwind
    ├── Skeleton / Skeleton Svelte
    ├── fonts
    ├── plugins / dark variant
    └── imports ../lib/styles/svelteforge-theme.css

src/lib/styles/svelteforge-theme.css
└── complete Skeleton v5 theme and visual source of truth
```

`src/lib/styles/svelteforge-theme.css` owns Skeleton-supported global visual decisions: palettes, surfaces, brand, root backgrounds, typography, radius/shapes, borders, rings and outlines.

There is intentionally no generic `tokens.css` or `index.css` style barrel in the scaffold. For local structure and whitespace, use standard Tailwind utilities such as `p-4`, `gap-6`, `space-y-8`, `max-w-7xl` and responsive variants.

Before adding global CSS or custom design tokens, ask whether Skeleton can express the requirement through its theme, presets or utilities. If it can, use Skeleton. Add a project-specific token/effects layer only later when a concrete repeated product need is not covered by Skeleton/Tailwind.

## Components

Canonical shared components live under:

```text
src/lib/components/svforge/
├── primitives/
├── ui/
└── layout/
```

For richer UI such as dialogs, tabs, tooltips, accordions, menus and date pickers, prefer direct imports from `@skeletonlabs/skeleton-svelte` rather than reimplementing them.

## AI workflow

Generated projects include:

- `AGENTS.md`
- `.svforge.json`
- `llms.txt`
- `svforge-catalog.json`
- `svforge-modules.json`
- `svforge-check.mjs`

Expected workflow:

```text
feature request
    ↓
read AGENTS.md + llms.txt + .svforge.json
    ↓
inspect existing components/modules
    ↓
compose with SvelteForge + Skeleton
    ↓
use the Skeleton theme for global visual changes
    ↓
svforge check + svelte-check + tests + build
```

## Commands

```bash
npx sv create my-app
cd my-app
npx sv add svforge=template:base+testing:vitest

# or
npx sv add svforge=template:dashboard+testing:vitest
```

```bash
svforge check
svforge context
svforge upgrade base
svforge upgrade dashboard
```

## Modules

Optional modules include realtime, audit, notifications, jobs, chat, email, uploads, oauth, blog, tiptap, dnd, graph and Skeleton-based toast feedback. Modules compose with the base/dashboard conventions instead of creating parallel architecture.
